walkthroughs.body_html:
Dualism (Plato, Descartes) — body and soul are separate. The soul survives death.

Materialism — only physical matter exists; consciousness dies with the brain.

The Christian and Muslim hope is bodily resurrection, not just survival of soul. 'God will give you a new body' (1 Corinthians 15:38).

Atheists argue:

1. Brain damage destroys personality — so no soul.
2. Hope of heaven is wishful thinking (Freud, Marx).
3. No reliable evidence of an afterlife.

Believers reply: love, consciousness and moral conscience point beyond the material. Jesus' resurrection is taken as historical evidence by Christians (1 Corinthians 15:3-8).

Traditional Christian view: hell is eternal conscious separation from God.

Annihilationism (held by some): the wicked cease to exist.

Universalism (e.g. some contemporary theologians): all are ultimately saved through Christ.

Islamic teaching: Jahannam is severe, but Allah is also Most Merciful — some traditions hold that some Muslim sinners may eventually leave Hell.

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.
The Buddha created the universe.

Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five steps of one cosmological argument.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.

Five distinct arguments for God's existence: from motion, causation, contingency, gradation of being, and final causes/teleology — collectively forming Aquinas's natural theology, not a single argument.
